argument: 17-magic-items.qmd:356 gives the Spellguard Shield, a Type: Shield card, a passive that grants DR 2. The canon home for a hero's DR is not this chapter: 16-armor-shields.qmd:13 and its own shield worked example at :108 both state the number is trained, never worn, and 15-equipment.qmd:221 repeats that the reduction comes from talents and abilities rather than armour. 09-talents-abilities.qmd:59-63 puts the only shipped hero DR ladder (2/5/8) on the Iron Skin talent, and the locked shield convention bars a shield from granting DR at all (convention 6). So this row is an exception that re-opens a DR source the rest of the book closes. Note the magnitude 2 sits exactly at the Novice Weak value, so it would not collapse damage tiers: the defect is the source of the DR, not the size of the number. Adamantine Plate at 17-magic-items.qmd:380 makes the same move from armour and is worth the council's parallel attention.

evidence.claim: The Spellguard Shield is typed as a shield and its passive grants DR 2.
The armour chapter states hero DR comes from training rather than from worn gear, making armour an illegal DR source.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Damage Reduction comes from your talents, not from your gear

evidence.claim: Its own shield worked example says the shield's value is Shield Block while the DR is attributed to Iron Skin, not the shield.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: the DR comes from Iron Skin and not from the board

evidence.claim: Iron Skin carries the shipped hero DR ladder, opening at 2 at Novice rank.
The equipment chapter restates that the DR number comes from talents and abilities, not armour.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: comes from your talents and abilities, not from your armor
